summary: A server-rendered Python website on Django with its ORM, admin, forms and migrations, served by gunicorn and tested against a real database.
description: Start a Django site that renders HTML on the server. Settings come from environment variables with validated defaults, and production refuses to start without a secret key. One notes app proves the shape: a model and its migration, an admin page, and a form that re-renders with inline errors or redirects after a save. A custom user model exists from the first migration. Every request is logged with an id, and a health view answers the serve probe. Checks cover ruff, djLint, strict mypy, pytest-django, missing migrations and Django's deployment checklist. Data lives in SQLite; Postgres, sign-in pages and background jobs are left to the project.
seoDescription: A Django web app recipe: ORM, admin, forms, migrations, pytest-django tests, structlog request logs, and gunicorn with whitenoise, managed with uv and make.

projectExamples.title: Internal records app with an admin
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace notes with the team's own records, edit them through Django's admin and a few forms, and keep the migration and test shape. Sign-in pages for non-staff users are work the project still adds.

plain.whatItIs: A starter Python website built with Django, where the server makes each page and a built-in admin area lets staff edit the stored records.
goodAt: Sites where people fill in forms and see saved records
Internal tools that need an admin area quickly
Projects that want database changes tracked step by step
notGoodAt: JSON APIs for apps or other programs; choose python-api.
Pages that update live without reloading; you add htmx or a frontend yourself.
Busy sites with many servers sharing data; move to Postgres first.
